questions.question: Who became the first wheelchair user to travel to space on a suborbital mission conducted by Blue Origin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Michaela Benthaus.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **German engineer Michaela Benthaus became the first person with paraplegia to travel to space.**
 
• **The journey was conducted by Jeff Bezos’ space tourism company Blue Origin.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Michaela Benthaus is a German engineer associated with the European Space Agency (ESA).**
 
• **She became the first wheelchair user to visit space.**
 
• **The mission was Blue Origin’s 16th crewed flight.**
 
• **The suborbital flight reached an altitude of about 100 km and lasted around 11 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Blue Origin**__ is a space tourism company founded by Jeff Bezos.
 
• The flight was carried out using the New Shepard NS-37 spacecraft.
 
• Passengers experienced brief weightlessness during the suborbital mission.
 
• The milestone marks a significant step forward for inclusivity and accessibility in space travel.

questions.question: Which upcoming Indian Antarctic research station is planned to replace the Maitri station and is targeted for completion by 2032?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maitri II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **India is developing Maitri II as its next-generation research station in East Antarctica, expected to be completed by 2032.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Maitri II will replace Maitri I**, which has been operational since 1989 in the Schirmacher Oasis of East Antarctica.
 
• **The project cost is estimated at ₹2,000 crore**, with **₹29.20 crore already approved** by the Ministry of Earth Sciences for pre-investment activities.
 
• **The station will focus on climate science, glaciology, biology, and earth sciences**, strengthening India’s long-term polar research capacity.
 
• **Maitri II will become India’s fourth Antarctic research station**, marking a major upgrade in scientific infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **India’s Antarctic programme began in 1981** with the establishment of **Dakshin Gangotri**, which ceased operations around 1989.
 
• **India currently operates two permanent Antarctic stations**: Maitri (East Antarctica) and Bharati (near the coast).
 
• **Maitri II will significantly enhance India’s polar presence** and support long-duration, advanced scientific research in Antarctica.

questions.question: Where were India's first 3-nanometre (3nm) chip design centres inaugurated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengaluru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Union Minister for Electronics & Information Technology, Railways, and Information & Broadcasting, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw today inaugurated two new state-of-the-art design facilities of Renesas Electronics India Private Limited, located in Noida and Bengaluru.
 
• Highlighting the uniqueness of the new facility, Shri Vaishnaw informed that this is India’s first design center to work on cutting-edge 3 nanometer chip design, a milestone that places India firmly in the global league of semiconductor innovation.
 
• To further strengthen the semiconductor ecosystem, the Government of India has been actively encouraging the development of semiconductor design centres in India.
 
• The Minister announced the launch of a new semiconductor learning kit aimed at enhancing practical hardware skills among engineering students.
 
• He also said that 270+ academic institutions that have already received advanced EDA (Electronic, Design, Automation) software tools under the India Semiconductor Mission will also receive these hands-on hardware kits.

questions.question: What is a Wolf Supermoon observed in January 2026?

options.text: A full moon in January that coincides with the Moon’s closest approach to Earth
A lunar eclipse occurring in January
The first new moon of the year in January
A meteor shower visible during January nights

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A full moon in January that coincides with the Moon’s closest approach to Earth.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **The January 2026 Wolf Supermoon occurred recently, appearing slightly larger and brighter than a normal full moon.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Wolf Moon refers to the full moon occurring in January, historically named after winter folklore with wolves.**
 
• Supermoon occurs when a full moon coincides with the Moon’s closest approach to Earth (perigee), making it appear larger and brighter.
 
• The Moon follows an elliptical orbit, with apogee as the farthest point and perigee as the closest point to Earth.
 
• Wolf Supermoon combines the Wolf Moon and Supermoon phenomena, leading to enhanced visual brightness and apparent size.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Moon Illusion__: The apparent enlargement of the Moon near the horizon due to human perception, not actual size change.
 
• __Lunar Terms__: Wolf Moon is a traditional name for January’s full moon, part of folklore-based full moon naming system.
 
• __Supermoon Characteristics__: Appears brighter and slightly larger than average full moons due to proximity to Earth.
 
• __Elliptical Orbit__: The Moon’s orbit is not perfectly circular, causing variations in distance from Earth—key for supermoon occurrence.

questions.question: When did NISAR begin its commissioning phase ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**After 1 year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar)** is an Earth observation satellite jointly developed by NASA and ISRO.
 
• The satellite is designed to monitor Earth's ecosystem, measure biomass, and study environmental changes.
 
• The commissioning phase of NISAR begins **1 year post-launch**, allowing adequate time for calibration and testing of onboard systems.
 
• During the commissioning phase, the satellite undergoes rigorous validation processes to ensure it meets performance metrics.
 
• The satellite's primary mission includes measuring changes in Earth's surface and providing data on natural disasters like earthquakes, floods, and landslides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Immediately after launch**

 
 
• This is incorrect because satellites like NISAR require an initial period for orbit stabilization and system checks before entering the commissioning phase.
 
• Post-launch activities include deployment of solar panels, stabilization, and initial health checks.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: After 90 days post-launch**
 
 
• Although many satellites undergo preliminary testing within 90 days, NISAR's commissioning phase is scheduled after a longer duration to ensure all systems are finely tuned.
 
• In this phase, initial data from the satellite is used for calibration but is not fully operational for scientific purposes.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: After 6 months**
 
 
• While 6 months is a reasonable timeframe for some satellites to enter commissioning, NISAR requires extensive system calibration due to its complex radar systems.
 
• Its sophisticated dual-frequency radar (L-band and S-band) necessitates more time for testing and validation.
 
 
 
• **About NISAR:**
 
 
• NISAR is equipped with the first dual-frequency radar system to monitor Earth's surface with unprecedented precision.
 
• The data provided by NISAR will be used for applications in agriculture, forestry, hydrology, and disaster management.
 
• The satellite's collaboration between NASA and ISRO represents a significant milestone in international space cooperation.

questions.question: NASA is set to launch Artemis II in 2026, its first crewed mission to the Moon since __________ in 1972.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Apollo 17.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **NASA is preparing for the launch of Artemis II in 2026, marking its first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Apollo 17 was the last crewed Moon mission conducted by NASA.**
 
• **The Apollo 17 mission took place in 1972.**
 
• **Artemis II marks the return of humans to lunar missions after over five decades.**
 
• **The mission will test systems critical for future Moon landings.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Apollo 17__

 __
 
• The final mission of NASA’s Apollo program.
 
• Featured astronauts Eugene Cernan, Harrison Schmitt, and Ronald Evans.
 
 
 
• Artemis Program__
 __
 
• NASA’s program aimed at returning humans to the Moon.
 
• Serves as a stepping stone for future Mars exploration.
 
 
 
• Crewed Lunar Missions__
 
 
• Involve human astronauts traveling beyond Earth orbit.
 
• Require extensive testing of spacecraft and life-support systems.

questions.question: ‘PARAM SHAKTI’, recently launched at IIT Madras, is significant because it

options.text: Hosts the indigenous PARAM RUDRA supercomputing system
Is India’s first exascale computing facility
Operates exclusively on proprietary foreign software

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hosts the indigenous PARAM RUDRA supercomputing system.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **MeitY__ launched the __PARAM SHAKTI__ supercomputing facility at __IIT Madras__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **PARAM SHAKTI__ hosts the indigenous __PARAM RUDRA__ supercomputing cluster.**
 
• **The system is developed and implemented by __C-DAC__ under the __National Supercomputing Mission (NSM)__.**
 
• **It delivers a peak computing capacity of __3.1 petaflops__, enabling over __3.1 quadrillion calculations per second__.**
 
• **The facility is __fully developed and manufactured in India__ and runs on __open-source software__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **PARAM RUDRA**__ – Built using __C-DAC’s indigenous RUDRA series of servers__, strengthening India’s self-reliance in high-performance computing.
 
• __**National Supercomputing Mission (NSM)**__ – Aims to enhance __research capacity__ and __computational infrastructure__ across academic and R&D institutions.
 
• __**Petaflop**__ – A unit of computing speed equal to __one quadrillion floating-point operations per second__.
 
• __**Significance**__ – Enables __large-scale simulations__, reduces dependence on prolonged experimental trials, and __accelerates research timelines__.

questions.question: Tata Lockheed Martin Aerostructures Limited delivered the 250th empennage (tail component) for which aircraft in December 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**C-130J Super Hercules**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tata Lockheed Martin Aerostructures Limited (TLMAL)** achieved a significant milestone by delivering the **250th empennage (tail component)** for the **C-130J Super Hercules** aircraft in December 2025.
 
• The **C-130J Super Hercules** is a **military transport aircraft** designed and manufactured by **Lockheed Martin Corporation**, a leading aerospace company based in the **United States**.
 
• The empennage is a **critical structural component** of the aircraft that includes the **vertical and horizontal stabilizers**. It plays a key role in ensuring the aircraft's **stability and control** during flight.
 
• India’s partnership with Lockheed Martin strengthens its capabilities in **aerospace manufacturing** and highlights its participation in the **global defense supply chain**.
 
• The C-130J Super Hercules is widely recognized for its **versatility** and has applications in **military, humanitarian, and disaster relief missions**, making it a critical asset for many nations worldwide.
 
• Tata Lockheed Martin Aerostructures Limited is a joint venture between **Tata Advanced Systems Limited** and **Lockheed Martin Corporation**, showcasing India’s growth in **defense manufacturing and technology collaboration.**
 
• This achievement reflects India’s ability to manufacture advanced **aerospace components** and contributes to the “**Make in India**” initiative, promoting domestic production of defense equipment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tejas**__

 __
 
• **Tejas** is an **Indian-made fighter jet** developed by the **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)**.
 
• It is a **lightweight, multi-role aircraft** designed for the Indian Air Force and Navy.
 
• The Tejas program reflects India’s progress in **indigenous defense technology**.
 
 
 
• **Rafale**__
 __
 
• **Rafale** is a **French-made multi-role fighter jet** developed by **Dassault Aviation**.
 
• It is known for its **advanced avionics, weaponry, and maneuverability**.
 
• India purchased Rafale jets to enhance its **air defense capabilities**.
 
 
 
• **Sukhoi Su-30MKI**__
 
 
• **Sukhoi Su-30MKI** is a **multi-role fighter aircraft** developed by **Russia** and customized for the Indian Air Force.
 
• It is manufactured under license by **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)** in India.
 
• Known for its **long-range, air superiority, and ground attack capabilities**, it plays a vital role in India’s defense strategy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an outcome associated with the Gaganyaan mission?

options.text: Strengthening international cooperation in space research
Improving India’s capability for crewed missions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lowering global surface temperatures**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Gaganyaan mission** is India's ambitious human spaceflight program developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (**ISRO**). Its primary goal is to demonstrate the capability of sending humans to space and safely returning them to Earth.
 
• The mission focuses on **enhancing indigenous human spaceflight technology**, which includes developments in crew modules, environmental control systems, and space-grade technologies. *Hence, this is an outcome of the Gaganyaan mission.*
 
• It also aims to **strengthen India's capability for crewed missions** by achieving self-reliance in human spaceflight technologies and making India the fourth nation to achieve this feat after the USA, Russia, and China. *Hence, this is an outcome of the Gaganyaan mission.*
